newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends a bit lower in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends a bit lower in line with JGBs.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract settled slightly lower on Monday, in line with a slight decline in Japanese government bonds, a rise in Tokyo share prices and weakness in the yen against the dollar.
But trade was thin ahead of much-awaited industrial output data due for release on Wednesday.
"The focus is on forecasts for manufacturers' output in July and August," a city bank trader said.

"The market has not yet formed a consensus on how the forecasts might turn out... But we feel the forecast for July will probably come in at around plus 0.9 percent and we are hoping that the forecast for August will be relatively weak," the city bank trader said.
Another city bank trader said the March could make a try for 99.20 if the forecasts for manufacturers' output in July and August turned out to be weak.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 100 billion yen from the money market on Monday morning against a projected fund surplus of 390 billion yen.
Key overnight call money was most actively traded at 0.48 percent on Monday, unchanged from Friday's weighted average, traders said.
Strong month-end fund-raising needs as well as healthy demand for short-end funds was preventing the key rate from declining despite the BOJ's accommodative stance, they said.
Borrowers do not want to raise funds by issuing certificates of deposit (CDs) at present because they feel CD rates will fall further, the first trader said.
About 50 billion yen worth of the key three-month CDs were issued at 0.65 percent on Monday.
The three-month CD rate was down slightly from 0.66 percent on Friday.

"Borrowers want to see CD rates fall more before they start raising funds by issuing CDs in earnest. Lenders, on the other hand, are reluctant to lend at lower rates, perhaps because they feel that fund demand ahead of corporate book-closings in September will pick up soon," a trader for another city bank said.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.58 percent, down from 0.59 percent on Friday, while two-month CDs were offered at 0.59 percent, flat from Friday.
